decision: matched the run to the Feature playbook, not the multi-phase-plan playbook
why: the brief asks for built code and one pull request; the multi-phase playbook delivers a plan and forbids implementing
result: Feature steps opened, run once per unit

decision: the critique stage of the how skill is unavailable
why: upstream pstack 1.4.0 removed the critique mode and its role; the brief still asks for critics
evidence: .claude/pstack-models.md, section The how critics row is gone
result: explorers and explainer run, critics stage skipped

decision: asked the founder how units 11, 12 and 13 handle the three missing surfaces
why: the checkout, the funded turn and the publish flow do not exist, and the brief made this a gate before the design arena
result: founder chose split per id with no new harness machinery

decision: sent three read-only explorer lanes over the harness, the database and edge functions, and the notifications emitter
why: the design must sit on measured facts, not on the brief's summary of them
result: running

decision: the brief says twenty-five ids are in the run, but its thirteen units name all twenty-seven
why: counted every Verify line in the units against the manifest's coverage check
result: the red set comes from the founder's per-id ruling, not from the brief's count

decision: explorer over the harness returned complete and provider-verified
why: the design must know how a new suite registers and what a declared red looks like
result: there is no time travel at the integration tier

decision: the daily reset must be computed at read time against a stored UTC day key
why: a scheduled job cannot be proven once per UTC day at integration, because no live adapter takes the harness clock
result: open, goes to the arena as a fixed direction

decision: explorer over the notifications emitter and the public surfaces returned complete and provider-verified
why: unit 3 emits through the emitter and unit 10 sweeps public surfaces
result: two hard constraints found

decision: the vet write and its emit run in one product definer function
why: the emit function revokes execute from public and grants nothing to the service role, so an edge function cannot call it
result: open, goes to the arena

decision: the vet record needs its own table with not-null columns, not a row on the audit table
why: the audit kind is a Postgres enum and its detail column is free jsonb, so nothing would stop a partial vet from committing
result: open, goes to the arena

decision: vet and unvet stay one taxonomy event and carry the outcome in the params
why: the taxonomy is closed and its oracle is asserted both ways by the notifications suite, so a new event type is a spec change
result: settled

decision: ran a four-lane design arena, one distinct structural direction per lane
why: the brief fixes the four lanes of the sheet and asks that the candidates not converge
result: three lanes returned, one lost its work

decision: set the red set at five ids, not the two the brief expected
why: walked each id against the tree: two need the fuel checkout, two need the publish flow, one needs both the checkout and funded-turn billing
result: twenty-two green, five red, told to the founder

decision: units 12 and 13 ship decision modules even though every id they carry is red
why: the tree already does this: the Discovery-message row of the write-route inventory is a stand-in that ships the decision a future route consults
result: settled, no new harness machinery

decision: the astra lane lost its design and was re-run
why: the prompt told a read-only lane to write a file; the sandbox refused and its short summary took the output slot
result: re-run in flight with the instruction corrected

decision: both external lanes lost their designs and both were re-run
why: the shared prompt told every lane to write its document to a file, but an external lane runs read-only and the runner then overwrites that path with the model's closing message
evidence: receipt-arena-1.json, receipt-arena-3.json, the two 3-line and 7-line files
result: grok had written 768 lines and they are not recoverable

decision: the rule for a future run: an external read-only lane returns its artifact as its reply, never as a file write
why: the runner reserves the output path and writes the final response there at completion, so anything the model puts at that path is destroyed
result: prompt corrected on both re-runs

decision: two candidates in, and they disagree at the centre
why: one stores spend in its own table keyed by organisation and UTC day; the other puts six columns on the organisations table and adds no table at all
result: open, the judge and the lead decide

decision: a second candidate reached the same five red ids independently
why: the lead derived the set by hand from the acceptance file and the allowance candidate derived it from the tree
result: corroborated, one candidate proposes a sixth red at the integration tier only

decision: paused at the founder's word at the end of the design arena, before the pick
why: the five-hour session limit is near and the next step, judging four candidates, is not a step to start and abandon
result: four candidates on disk, none judged

decision: dispatched the cross-judge blinded, on four files named A to D
why: the judge's own family wrote one of the four candidates, and the pool has no lane that did not
result: running

decision: found a gap the acceptance file does not decide: what an unvet does to credits already granted that day
why: one candidate claws them back by recomputing, another keeps them by storing the remainder, and no acceptance id names the case
result: open, needs a founder call if the judge does not settle it

decision: proposed a shape no candidate wrote: store credits spent and the highest grant applied today
why: it gives both properties from one number, so an unvet cannot lower the mark and a re-vet cannot raise it past thirty, with no stored boolean to remember
result: candidate for the graft

decision: the judge picked the vetting-aggregate candidate as the base, and the lead agrees
why: it is the only candidate whose completeness rule is a schema fact rather than a guard every caller must go through
result: base settled, twenty of thirty against seventeen, seventeen and twelve

decision: the lead was wrong about the clock and the judge was right
why: a transaction that starts before midnight can take its lock after midnight, so transaction-start time charges the spend to the wrong day
result: the build takes the clock after the lock

decision: the founder ruled that an unvetted organisation keeps the credits it already holds until the next UTC day
why: no acceptance id settles the case, and all four candidates chose silently and differently
result: settled, and it removes the stored raise flag entirely

decision: the red set grows from five ids to eight
why: the judge showed every candidate promoting partial coverage to green, and the founder's per-id ruling applied honestly produces eight
result: nineteen green at integration, twenty at loop

decision: wrote the design of record as a base plus seven grafts and five corrections
why: the arena produces one synthesized artifact, and rewriting eight hundred lines to restate a base nobody disputes would waste the run
result: design phase closed, build starts

decision: deleted the blinded copies of the four candidates
why: they were my own scratch copies for the judge, and the originals and the verdict are committed
result: removed

decision: one owner, units in the brief's fixed order, no parallel writers
why: every unit writes the same six shared files, the manifest among them, and a manifest cannot be split, so parallel lanes would spend more time in conflicts than they save
result: throughput checkpoint written

decision: started the local Supabase stack
why: the integration tier needs it and starting it early keeps it off the critical path
evidence: db:start exit 0, no key material printed
result: up

decision: the suite scaffold goes to the hardest-tasks lane, not the feature lane
why: it designs the suite seam that all thirteen units inherit, which is a one-way door, and the brief sends a unit here only when the writer must still design something
result: running on fable at medium

decision: the scaffold writes no product code and every id it registers is red
why: a suite that compiles and reports twenty-seven honest reds is the blocking first step, and mixing product code into it would hide which unit proved what
result: running

decision: the suite scaffold landed and every one of the six checks passes
why: twenty-seven call sites in bijection with the acceptance file, and the manifest declares all of them red at both tiers
result: green, lead re-ran all six checks itself

decision: the allowance is a deployed route, not only a database function
why: the scaffold's contract chose it and the lead accepts it: it buys a real deployed-boundary proof for the grant and the two gate ids, where the alternative was operator SQL
result: settled, costs one write-route row and the auth-suite map edits

decision: one lane worktree for all fourteen units, reset between them, not one worktree each
why: a worktree cannot be removed without a founder decision, so fourteen of them would accumulate for no gain
result: branch renamed, worktree reused

decision: the run stopped after unit zero for no reason and the founder asked why
why: the lead ended its turn at a reporting boundary when nothing needed a founder answer, against the brief's instruction to run the item end to end
evidence: this trail, the turn after commit d2e913f
result: corrected, units continue without stopping between them

decision: unit one goes to the feature lane, not the hardest-tasks lane
why: the table, the constraints and the definer body are all specified in the design of record, so the writer applies a fixed contract and designs nothing
result: running on grok at xhigh

decision: unit one implements both the vet and the unvet state change, but no notification
why: the two branches are one symmetric function, so splitting them would make unit three rewrite it instead of inserting the emit into it
result: unit three adds the emit only

decision: the founder ruled that a unit boundary notifies but never blocks
why: the founder proposed a blocking question per unit for compaction control, and the lead argued that thirteen stalls cost more than they buy once every boundary is cheap to resume from
result: settled, one notification per unit and no gate

decision: the per-unit loop gains a checkpoint write
why: a rewritten resume note after each unit makes an interrupt safe at any moment, not only at a boundary, because a writer lane commits nothing
result: folded into the loop

decision: the vetting record landed and all eight checks pass
why: the lead re-ran every check itself, including both integration tiers, rather than taking the writer's report
result: two ids green at both tiers

decision: kept the seat-holder and email checks the definer makes, although nothing emits yet
why: the brief asked for a shape that lets unit three insert the emit rather than rewrite the function, and these two reads are that seam
result: accepted, unit three must cover both refusals with a test

decision: checked that the schema arm probes each mandated column separately
why: the writer reported that a null trips the organisation key first, which would have proved only the primary key
result: eleven columns, one at a time, correct

decision: the unit two lane was cancelled sixteen minutes in, not failed
why: the grok CLI reported a user cancellation on a check command; the lead did not cancel it and the cause is outside the run
evidence: receipt-unit2.json, status malformed-output, stop reason cancelled
result: dropout recorded, about fifty cents spent

decision: ran the checks on the abandoned tree instead of rerunning the writer
why: the brief says a writer that dies after finishing its work is recovered by running the checks and committing the tree
evidence: the lane worktree, six files changed
result: the suite failed at both tiers, so the work was not finished after all

decision: diagnosed the failure as a body that never opens a fixture world
why: the harness refuses any body that returns without opening a world, and the manual-only id was written as source oracles alone
result: fix specified by the lead

decision: gave the five-line fix to the mechanical agent with the assertion written out, not to another feature lane
why: the cause was fully diagnosed and the precedent named, so a sixteen-minute writer lane would buy nothing
result: running

decision: unit two landed after the lead diagnosed and specified the fix
why: the cancelled writer left a suite that failed at both tiers, and running the checks rather than trusting the tree is what caught it
result: four ids green at both tiers
